title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1LC1RE_1LA1RC_1RA0LC_0RF---_0LD1RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1LC1RE_1LA1RC_1RA0LC_0RF---_0LD1RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The pieces of a sweep are proved in Lean for every size (leftward recoding of even blocks into pairs, the turn at an odd block, the rightward regrouping of pairs by threes); the global dynamics, a few defects drifting through a background of 1^8 blocks, is described from simulation only. No halt in the first 1011 steps (The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c runs 1011 steps from blank tape without a halt (522,424 cells visited).).

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The pieces of a sweep
claims.text: For every k and every surrounding tape: leftward, an even block 1^(2k+2) becomes the segment (1 0)^k 1 0 0 and C moves on (left_even); an odd block 1^(2k+1) becomes the same kind of segment, glues two 1s to the block on its left and turns the head right (left_odd); rightward, every three pairs 1 0 1 0 1 0 become 1^5 0 (right_group) and a segment end 1 0 0 met in phase 0 becomes 1 1 1 (right_seg0).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>11</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c runs 1011 steps from blank tape without a halt (522,424 cells visited).

claims.title: Blocks of 3d+2, defects in a background of 1^8
claims.text: At the right-end moments of the first 3·107 steps every block right of the start cell but the first (cut at the start cell) and the last (3) has 3d+2 ones; 1^8 (d = 2) is the background: its 3 pairs plus segment end regroup to 1^5 plus 3 = 1^8 again. A handful of defects (digit groups such as 4 1, 7, 1 5, 3 1, 6, 1 2 1) sit between long runs of 8s; the runs to their left shrink and those to their right grow by one per pass, so the defects drift left, and the leftmost group of digits changes slowly, like the top digits of a counter.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open. A proof would need the rules for every phase of the rightward pass and a closed description of how defects move, collide and are created; the dynamics is a recoding between halving and grouping by threes, of the Collatz-like kind.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine rewrites its tape back and forth between two codes: going left it halves blocks of 1s into pairs, going right it regroups the pairs three at a time. Blocks of eight 1s survive the round trip unchanged, so the tape fills with them, and a few irregular blocks drift through them like particles.

facts.text: The pieces of a sweep, proved in Lean for every size.
Blocks of 3d+2 ones; a few defects drift left.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.484).
After 109 steps the tape spans 49,170 cells (55 left of the start, 39,295 right), with a density of 1s of 0.874.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Two ways to write the same tape
html: Each time the head reaches the right end, the right part of the tape (from the start cell on) is a row of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, and apart from the first one (cut at the start cell, written in brackets) and a last block of 3, every block has 3d + 2 ones: 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, ... Most of them are 1^8. We write a block by its digit d, so the tape after 23,657,027 steps reads [6] 1 2^31 1 2^122 1 2^199 4 2^46 6 2^502 0: a piece of 6 ones at the start cell, then long runs of 8s (digit 2) with a few other digits in between.
The machine keeps rewriting the tape between this block form and a pair form made of pairs 1 0. An even block and the 0 after it, 1^(2k+2) 0, has the same length as 0 0 (1 0)^k 1:

Going from one form to the other is halving (2k + 2 ones give k pairs); going back is grouping pairs by three. The machine is a two-way translator between those two codes.

sections.heading: Left: halve; right: group by threes
html: Leftward pass. State C walks left. An even block is rewritten into its pair form (left_even, about 2 steps per cell) and C carries on to the next block. The first odd block stops it: it is rewritten too, two 1s are glued to the block on its left, and the head turns right (left_odd).

Rightward pass. States B, C, D walk right through the pairs and rebuild blocks: every three pairs 1 0 1 0 1 0 become 1^5 0 (right_group), and the end of a segment, 1 0 0, adds three more 1s when it is met in step (right_seg0). So a block of eight, written as three pairs and a segment end, comes back as 5 + 3 = 8: 1^8 is a fixed point of the round trip, which is why the tape fills with 8s.

A segment end met out of step (after one pair of a group) sends the head left again before it reaches the right end: then a new leftward pass starts in the middle of the tape. Blocks other than 8 do not survive the round trip unchanged; they are the defects.

sections.heading: Defects drifting through a sea of 8s
html: Snapshots of the digit form, each about 6·105 steps apart (the head at the right end):

Between the runs of 8s sit a few small groups of other digits. Each group cycles through a few shapes (1 2 1, 1 5, 3 1, 6, 4 1, 7, ...) and, as it does, the run of 8s to its left shrinks and the one to its right grows: the defects drift left, the rightmost one fastest. The rightmost run grows by about one block per pass, which is the square-root growth of the tape. When a defect reaches the group at the left, that group changes, like the leading digits of a counter. The part of the tape left of the start cell is short and stops growing (the fixed side).

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is E reading a 1, and E is entered only from B reading a 1. In the rightward pass B reads the 1 of a pair 1 0 and E then reads its 0, so the machine would halt only if B met two 1s in a row: a rightward pass running into block form instead of pair form. The rules proved so far never do that; whether some collision of defects ever produces it is not known.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean, kernel (lean/Passes.lean, generated by py/gen_rules.py with bbtools.symtm): left_even, left_odd, right_group, right_seg0, each for every k and every surrounding tape; the halting configurations and no halt in 10,000 steps (lean/Blank.lean). Lean, native_decide: no halt in 107 steps.
Open: the rightward pass out of step and the rules for the defects, and the question itself.

family: base-2/base-3 recoding: blocks 1^(3d+2), travelling defects in a background of 1^8
summary: The tape is blocks of 3d+2 ones, mostly 1^8; each leftward pass recodes even blocks into pairs (halving) and each rightward pass regroups the pairs by threes, so a few defects drift left through the 1^8 background like particles; open.
